strongest_results.name: growing-moment low-conductor spectral small deviation
strongest_results.statement: Normalize the ANOVA energies of W^q by M_2,q, where q=floor(s/a), s tends to infinity and s=o(log_3 X). The selected-prime coordinates are independent non-identical Bernoulli variables with theta_p=(1+o(1))H/p uniformly for p>=2H and total mean (1+o(1))HL. For every fixed alpha>0, conductor at most exp(alpha HL) forces only O_alpha(H) selected primes, and its normalized energy probability is at most exp(-(1-o(1))HL). Thus the unnormalized Fourier energy below that level is at most exp(-(2-o(1))HL).

strongest_results.name: deterministic primitive large-sieve cutoff
strongest_results.statement: Fix eta in (0,1), set alpha=1-eta, and then let X tend to infinity. On every prescribed interval of length N asymptotic to X, the signed aggregate over 1<c(T)<=exp((1-eta)HL) is at most exp(-(eta-o(1))HL). For H=(log X)^2 the cutoff is X^((1-eta+o(1)) log_1 X log_2 X). More generally the same proof works for every fixed H=(log X)^d, d>=1, with cutoff X^((1-eta+o(1))(log X)^(d-1) log_2 X) and candidate coefficient d.

strongest_results.name: candidate forces positive ultra-high signed tail
strongest_results.statement: If one original candidate lies in the interval, the exact signed aggregate over all primitive full conductors c(T)>exp((1-eta)HL) is positive and at least one half times t^(qR)=exp(-o(HL)). This is a necessary condition, not an upper bound or contradiction.

strongest_results.name: growing-moment exceptional-phase density
strongest_results.statement: For starts uniform modulo the full CRT period, the fraction of length-N intervals with moment sum at least t^(qR), hence the fraction that can contain a local candidate, is at most exp(-(1-o(1))HL). The period is much larger and exceptional starts can cluster for length N, so this does not locate the actual dyadic start.

strongest_results.name: fixed-moment Rankin transfer
strongest_results.statement: For fixed q,C, Rankin's trick gives conductor mass F(Y)<=z^K for Y<=Xz and transfers all conductors through D=N z^(-B), leaving only a fixed-power-in-z inherited suffix.

strongest_results.name: fixed-moment polynomial middle range
strongest_results.statement: For each prescribed fixed A, one may then choose fixed q with qC>A+1/2+delta and deterministically control D<c(T)<=X^A at the actual interval start. One fixed q does not control all A.

strongest_results.name: coefficient-one pooled energy ceiling
strongest_results.statement: The single pooled energy plus global worst-case Farey spacing plus physical Cauchy calculation gives exp((alpha-1+o(1))HL) at cutoff exp(alpha HL). Its cumulative nonconstant low-energy exponent is exactly 2HL already on the one-prime layers, so the energy gain is not a zero-mode artefact; this does not exclude conductor-stratified spacing estimates because those witnesses lie at smaller conductors. Put a CRT point with W^q=1 inside any length-X interval: positivity and the uniform low estimate force the high signed interval aggregate to be at least 1-o(1). Thus arbitrary-start interval smallness is false, though the CRT representative is not at the self-consistent location A asymptotic to X.

quantifier_order: Fix the original epsilon and fixed C.
Choose s(X) tending to infinity with s=o(log_3 X), and q=floor(s/a).
Fix eta in (0,1), then set alpha=1-eta.
Only afterward let X tend to infinity.
No simultaneous eta-to-zero statement is used.

next_round_conditional_interface.d_equals_2_specialization: At H=(log X)^2 and shifts k asymptotic to H, a #679 candidate has omega(n-k)<=(2+o_epsilon(1))(1+epsilon) log_2 X/log_3 X. It would suffice to force in every corresponding H-block one integer with omega>C0 log_2 X/log_3 X for a fixed C0>2(1+epsilon).
next_round_conditional_interface.relation_to_current_route: This is the same local-density bottleneck that the Fourier argument reduces to the ultra-high-conductor signed aggregate.

remaining_gap: Primary route: prove an upper bound o(t^(qR)) for the exact signed aggregate over c(T)>exp((1-eta)HL) at the prescribed actual start A asymptotic to X; energy, absolute coefficients, and arbitrary-CRT-start estimates do not provide this. Alternative sufficient route: prove Lau's unproved fixed-power short-interval density conjecture for integers with omega at least C0 log_2 x/log_3 x, with interval exponent d<C0.

literature_audit.result: Bettin-Chandee has a relevant inverse-modulus phase but no theorem stated for the ultra-high many-prime, growing-shift aggregate.
Wright 2026 removes no remaining mismatch in conductor structure, shifted dimension, or target normalization.
van Doorn-Tang reaches exp(Theta((log_2 X)^2)) rather than the required endpoint exp(log_1 X) at the relevant run length.

Tao-Teravainen v2 proves the weaker Erdős #248 bound Omega(n+k)<=Ck. Its Remark 1.2 explicitly states the #679 target and assesses it as beyond the present method; its O(log_2 X) simultaneous-shift sieve does not control the H=(log X)^2 ultra-high signed-conductor tail required here.

Lau v2 (2026-06-24), Theorem 1.3, unconditionally gives infinitely many n with omega(n-k)<=Omega(n-k)<=C log k for every 1<k<n, explicitly leaving a log log k factor to #679. Its predicted optimality and Section 7 falsity theorem depend on unproved conjectures and do not close #679.

verification.scope: Finite algebra and normalization only; no asymptotic claim depends on computation.
